arxiv-2107-00404.title: Search for new phenomena in three- or four-lepton events in p ​ p pp collisions at s = 13 \sqrt{s}=13 TeV with the ATLAS detector
arxiv-2107-00404.creator: The ATLAS Collaboration
arxiv-2107-00404.description: Abstract A search with minimal model dependence for physics beyond the Standard Model in events featuring three or four charged leptons ( 3 ​ ℓ 3\ell and 4 ​ ℓ 4\ell , ℓ = e , μ \ell=e,\mu ) is presented. The analysis aims to be sensitive to a wide range of potential new-physics theories simultaneously.

arxiv-2201-12514.title: Composing a surrogate observation operator for sequential data assimilation
arxiv-2201-12514.creator: Kosuke Akita, Yuto Miyatake, Daisuke Furihata
arxiv-2201-12514.description: Abstract In data assimilation, state estimation is not straightforward when the observation operator is unknown. This study proposes a method for composing a surrogate operator when the true operator is unknown. A neural network is used to improve the surrogate model iteratively to decrease the difference between the observations and the results of the surrogate model.

arxiv-2202-00792.title: AdaAnn: Adaptive Annealing Scheduler for Probability Density Approximation
arxiv-2202-00792.creator: Emma R. Cobian, Jonathan D. Hauenstein, Fang Liu, and Daniele E. Schiavazzi
arxiv-2202-00792.description: Abstract Approximating probability distributions can be a challenging task, particularly when they are supported over regions of high geometrical complexity or exhibit multiple modes. Annealing can be used to facilitate this task which is often combined with constant a priori selected increments in inverse temperature.

arxiv-2407-09972.title: MedLeak: Multimodal Medical Data Leakage in Secure Federated Learning with Crafted Models
arxiv-2407-09972.creator: Shanghao Shi, Md Shahedul Haque, Abhijeet Parida, Chaoyu Zhang, Marius George Linguraru, Y. Thomas Hou, Syed Muhammad Anwar, Wenjing Lou
arxiv-2407-09972.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Shanghao Shi, Md Shahedul Haque, Abhijeet Parida, Chaoyu Zhang, Marius George Linguraru, Y. Thomas Hou, Syed Muhammad Anwar, Wenjing Lou. Federated learning (FL) allows participants to collaboratively train machine learning models while keeping their data private, making it ideal for collaborations among healthcare institutions on sensitive datasets.

arxiv-2509-22114.title: SK 2 Decompile: LLM-based Two-Phase Binary Decompilation from Skeleton to Skin
arxiv-2509-22114.creator: Hanzhuo Tan, Weihao Li, Xiaolong Tian, Siyi Wang, Jiaming Liu, Jing Li, Yuqun Zhang
arxiv-2509-22114.description: Abstract Large Language Models (LLMs) have emerged as a promising approach for binary decompilation. However, the existing LLM-based decompilers are still somewhat limited in effectively presenting a program’s source-level structure with its original identifiers. To mitigate this, we introduce SK 2 Decompile , a novel two-phase approach to decompile from the skeleton (semantic structure) to the skin (identifier) of programs.

arxiv-2509-25380.title: Predicting Training Re-evaluation Curves Enables Effective Data Curriculums for LLMs
arxiv-2509-25380.creator: Shane Bergsma, Nolan Dey & Joel Hestness
arxiv-2509-25380.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Shane Bergsma, Nolan Dey & Joel Hestness. Data curriculums have become central to successful LLM training, yet principles governing optimal data placement remain unclear. We introduce the training re-evaluation curve (TREC) , a diagnostic that retrospectively evaluates training batches using the final model weights . The TREC characterizes how well a trained model retains training data as a function of when the data was encountered during training.

arxiv-2512-00763.title: Provable Benefit of Sign Descent: A Minimal Model Under Heavy-Tail Class Imbalance
arxiv-2512-00763.creator: Robin Yadav, Shuo Xie, Tianhao Wang, Zhiyuan Li
arxiv-2512-00763.description: Abstract Adaptive optimization methods (such as Adam) play a major role in LLM pretraining, significantly outperforming Gradient Descent (GD). Recent studies have proposed new smoothness assumptions on the loss function to explain the advantages of adaptive algorithms with structured preconditioners, e.g., coordinate-wise or layer-wise, and steepest descent methods w.r.t. non-euclidean norms, e.g.

arxiv-2512-18476.title: Lineshape-asymmetry-caused shift in atomic interferometers
arxiv-2512-18476.creator: V. I. Yudin, O. N. Prudnikov, A. V. Taichenachev, M. Yu. Basalaev, D. N. Kapusta, A. N. Goncharov, M. D. Radchenko, V. G. Pal’chikov, L. Zhou, M. S. Zhan
arxiv-2512-18476.description: Abstract We investigate the shift caused by asymmetry of spectroscopic lineshape in atomic interferometers, which has not previously been discussed in the scientific literature. This asymmetry arises because laser field is frequency-chirped not only during the free-evolution intervals of atoms, but also during the Ramsey pulses.

arxiv-2602-18212.title: Design and Characterization of a Dual-DOF Soft Shoulder Exosuit with Volume-Optimized Pneumatic Actuator
arxiv-2602-18212.creator: Rui Chen, Domenico Chiaradia, Daniele Leonardis, Antonio Frisoli
arxiv-2602-18212.description: Abstract Portable pneumatic systems for 2 degree-of-freedom (DOF) soft shoulder exosuits remain underexplored, and face fundamental trade-offs between torque output and dynamic response that are further compounded by the need for multiple actuators to support complex shoulder movement. pmc-12534941.title: The effect of remote ischemic conditioning combined with tirofiban on early neurological deterioration in small artery occlusive stroke
pmc-12534941.creator: Zhiyong Zhang, Xinxiu Liu, Lei Wang, Xunming Ji
pmc-12534941.description: ObjectivesEarly neurological deterioration (END) remains a significant challenge in the treatment of small artery occlusive (SAO) stroke. The purpose of this study was to evaluate the efficacy and safety of remote ischemic conditioning (RIC) combined with tirofiban for patients with SAO stroke experiencing END.

pmc-13051357.title: Apolipoprotein E (APOE) Promotes Cell Proliferation and Invasion in Glioma via the PI3K/AKT Signaling Pathway
pmc-13051357.creator: Mengdi Xia, Ke Chen, Weiwei Chen, Zhenhua Ren, Xiaohui Li
pmc-13051357.description: BackgroundGlioma presents significant therapeutic challenges due to its marked heterogeneity and resistance to conventional treatments. Apolipoprotein E (APOE), a glycoprotein involved in lipid metabolism, has been reported to be dysregulated in glioma; however, its functional role in glioma progression remains poorly understood.

pmc-13072462.title: Analysis of factors influencing patient delay in tuberculosis patients in Northeast China: surveillance data from 2015 to 2024
pmc-13072462.creator: Yuchen Gao, Jingxiao Li, Jiying Ma, Zihui Yu, Xiaohui Ren, Siwei Chao, Nan Wang, Jie Liu, Yu Wang
pmc-13072462.description: BackgroundTuberculosis (TB) remains a serious challenge to China’s public health, and timely detection and diagnosis of play key roles in preventing disease spread and deterioration. The aim of this study was to understand the delay in consultation for TB patients in Shenyang City, Liaoning Province, and to determine the factors that influence this delay.

pmc-13122895.title: Critical care resource disparities in China: a nationwide survey and policy recommendations for health equity
pmc-13122895.creator: Xijing Zhang, Yu Chen, Renhuai Liu, Wei Fang, Bingyu Qin, Ronglin Jiang, Yuan Gao, Wenxiong Li, Jianfeng Wu, Mingyan Zhao, Yi Yang, Xiaochun Ma, Bin Du, Jiao Liu, Xuan Song, Dong Zhang, Xinjing Gao, Xiaodong Jin, Jian Liu, Fen Liu, Lixia Liu, Jinghui Li, Siqing Ma, Zhiyong Peng, Yunbo Sun, Songjing
pmc-13122895.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundCritical care medicine plays a pivotal role in addressing life-threatening conditions; however, its development in China is hindered by resource scarcity and inequitable distribution. Existing studies have mostly focused on ICU bed numbers or selected regions, and have rarely provided a comprehensive, nationwide assessment of ICU beds, staffing and equipment using standardized methods, nor have they systematically quantified population-based equity of ICU resources.

pmc-13153150.title: An improved whale optimization algorithm for flexible job shop scheduling problems with machine deterioration effects
pmc-13153150.creator: Kun Li, Silong Tian
pmc-13153150.description: Targeting the characteristics of performance degradation caused by prolonged machine operation in real production, this article examines the flexible job shop scheduling problem under machine deterioration effects, develops the FJSP-MDE mathematical model to minimize makespan, and presents an Improved Whale Optimization Algorithm (IWOA) to solve the problem.

pmc-13330164.title: Er: YAG laser debonding performance for cement-retained zirconia implant crowns
pmc-13330164.creator: Xinyuan Zhang, Ziyang Yu, Qian Li, Xiaomin Wu, Chunlan Guo, Haitao Dong
pmc-13330164.description: BackgroundErbium laser debonding methods have been increasingly applied in natural tooth restorations and are highly important for the repair and maintenance of cement-retained implant restorations. However, the debonding process is challenging, and research on its safety, efficacy, and influencing factors remains insufficient.

pmc-13413184.title: Intracranial Hemorrhage After Reduction Malarplasty: A Narrative Review Focusing on Surgical Technique
pmc-13413184.creator: Myoung Soo Kim
pmc-13413184.description: Reduction malarplasty (RMP) is performed frequently in East Asia. Although various complications of RMP have been reported, intracranial hemorrhage has been described only rarely. Although intracranial hemorrhage is an extremely rare complication, it is a catastrophic event that should not occur in esthetic plastic surgery.

pmc-13548183.title: Beyond class switching in multi-refractory inflammatory bowel disease: Nine case reports and review of literature
pmc-13548183.creator: Jonathan Soldera, Maria Antonia Selbach Pertile, Leticia Nodari Carobin, Daniel Jun Funatsu Brambilla, Eduardo Brambilla
pmc-13548183.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). A clinically relevant subset of patients with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) remain partial responders despite multiple advanced therapies. In this setting, reflexive class switching risks forfeiting incremental mechanistic gains, whereas a deliberate “build-on-partial-response” strategy - through dose optimization, extended induction, and, in selected cases, advanced combination therapy (ACT) [an oral Janus kinase inhibitor (iJAK) plus a biologic] - may consolidate disease control.

pmc-13620416.title: Targeting the remodeled peritoneal ecosystem: a paradigm shift from tumor cells to the microenvironment in gastric cancer peritoneal metastasis
pmc-13620416.creator: Ya-xin Gong, Di Hao, Jia-hao Tan, Lu-ya Li, Jing Bai, Rui Feng
pmc-13620416.description: Peritoneal metastasis (PM) is the most common form of organ-specific metastasis in advanced gastric cancer (GC), and is driven by the dynamic interplay between cancer cells and the tumor microenvironment (TME). This review elaborates on the mechanisms through which cancer cells utilize metabolic reprogramming, mechanical stress, and neural control to shape the microenvironment conducive to tumor growth.

pmc-13632323.title: Effect of concomitant chemotherapy on edoxaban plasma concentration in patients with colorectal cancer
pmc-13632323.creator: Jihyung Song, Kei Kimura, Kozo Kataoka, Hirofumi Ota, Masayoshi Yasui, Taishi Hata, Takashi Daimon, Masataka Ikeda
pmc-13632323.description: PurposeDirect oral anticoagulants are a treatment option for cancer-associated venous thromboembolism (VTE). In patients receiving chemotherapy for cancer, there may be pharmacokinetic drug–drug interaction between anti-cancer agents and direct oral anticoagulants. However, there are no data available in patients with colorectal cancer (CRC). In this study, we investigated edoxaban plasma concentration in patients with CRC receiving chemotherapy.
